objective: Prove -- or honestly close -- the last unproven seam in the mission loop: real in-game clipboard text reaching the real engine. Every item this repo has ever calculated is in Path of Building EXPORT format (engine/tests/fixtures/item.txt). Real Ctrl+C text is a different shape: an 'Item Class:' header, '--------' separators, 'Rarity: Rare' capitalization, Requirements/Item Level blocks, '(implicit)'/'(crafted)' mod suffixes. grep -rl 'Item Class:' hits only overlay/. The overlay forwards captured text UNCHANGED on the stated contract that 'the server canonicalizes' (overlay/src/diffFlow.ts), yet server/calculator.py writes the bytes straight to a file for new('Item', readAll(path)) in engine/pobcalc.lua -- no canonicalization exists anywhere. (1) Add real game-clipboard fixtures under engine/tests/fixtures/game_clipboard/: at minimum a rare with the full header, an unidentified rare, and an influenced or corrupted item. Hand-write them to the game's exact shape. (2) Drive each through the real worker in engine/tests/test_server_adapter.py against the golden build that file already imports, keeping its loud-skip-when-runtime-absent policy. (3) For every fixture the engine reads: assert a schema-valid verdict card. For any fixture it CANNOT read: either add the minimal canonicalization at the server boundary in server/calculator.py -- a normalizer that converts game-format text to what PoB's parser accepts, unit-tested in tests/test_server.py without the runtime -- or, if the shape is genuinely out of reach inside this stage's budget, record it in engine/GAPS.md under Open with the exact failing line and open a follow-up issue. What you may NOT do is leave the behavior undescribed or let a real item silently become CANT_EVALUATE with no record. (4) tests/test_server.py must cover the boundary behavior with a stub calculator so the seam is checked on every CI run, runtime or not.
constraints: Canonicalization, if any, is a TEXT normalization at the server boundary only. Do not touch engine/pobcalc.lua, the vendored submodule, or the corpus (protected).
The normalizer must never invent, drop, or reinterpret a modifier value. If a line cannot be mapped, the item stays unreadable and the honest CANT_EVALUATE/422 path handles it (I5).
No contract change: /diff still takes raw item_text. If you believe the contract must change, stop and route it to pm; do not edit contracts/.
Existing tests may be EXTENDED, never deleted or skipped, and engine/tests/fixtures/item.txt stays byte-identical -- the parity and e2e suites pin it.
engine/tests/test_server_adapter.py keeps its runtime-availability skip: a missing runtime must skip loudly, never silently pass.
Stage PR uses 'Refs #119', never 'Fixes' (ADR-0008) unless every criterion on #119 is met by this diff.

acceptance_criteria.text: engine/tests/fixtures/game_clipboard/ holds at least three real-shape in-game clipboard items (full rare, unidentified, influenced or corrupted), each with the 'Item Class:' header and '--------' separators.

engine/tests/test_server_adapter.py drives every one of those fixtures through the real worker against the golden build and asserts, per fixture, a schema-valid verdict payload or an explicitly recorded unreadable outcome.

For every fixture the engine cannot read, either server/calculator.py canonicalizes it (with a runtime-free unit test in tests/test_server.py covering that exact text) or engine/GAPS.md records the failure under Open with the failing line and a filed issue number. No fixture is left undescribed.
tests/test_server.py passes without the engine runtime and covers the boundary behavior with a stub calculator.
engine/tests/fixtures/item.txt is byte-identical to its committed state and no existing test was deleted or skipped.
The PR states, in one line per fixture, what the real engine actually did with it -- the evidence the org has never had.

rollback: git revert the stage commit; fixtures and their tests disappear and the server boundary returns to passing item text through untouched.
